name: Basajaun
body:
Basajaun CR
5

This stocky giant is crowned in tangled waves of dark hair and a massive beard. His gnarled hands grip a fallen tree trunk as a cudgel.

XP 1,600
NG Large humanoid (giant)
Init +1; Senses low-light vision; Perception +12

DEFENSE

AC 16, touch 10, flat-footed 15 (+1 Dex, +6 natural, –1 size)
hp 66 (7d8+35)
Fort +10, Ref +3, Will +6

OFFENSE

Speed 40 ft.
Melee greatclub +12 (2d8+10) or slam +11 (1d6+10)
Space 10 ft.; Reach 10 ft.
Special Attacks backswing, walking stick percussion

STATISTICS

Str 24, Dex 12, Con 21, Int 17, Wis 19, Cha 18
Base Atk +5; CMB +11; CMD 22
Feats Cleave, Great Cleave, Power Attack, Weapon Focus (greatclub)
Skills Climb +11, Craft (carpentry, stonemasonry, weapons) +10, Knowledge (Nature) +9, Perception +12, Stealth +4, Survival +9
Languages Common, Druidic, Giant, Sylvan

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Backswing (Ex)

As a full-round action, a basajaun can attack one creature it threatens with its greatclub.

If the attack hits, the basajaun can make a combat maneuver check to trip the target. If the attack misses, the basajaun can instead make a combat maneuver check to bull rush a creature it threatens that is adjacent to the target of its greatclub attack.

Walking Stick Percussion (Ex)

As a full-round action, a basajaun can smash its greatclub against the ground. All creatures standing on the ground other than the basajaun in a 15-foot spread take 2d6 points of bludgeoning damage (DC 20 Reflex half), and creatures that fail their save fall prone. The save DC is Strength-based.

ECOLOGY

Environment forest (any)
Organization solitary or pair
Treasure standard (greatclub, other treasure)

Also known as bonjarau, basjarau, or bosnerau, these peaceful, hairy giants are often regarded as lords of small forest domains and watchful sentinels, calling out to shepherds to warn them when danger is nearby. As payment, those who live in or near a basajaun’s woods may leave out bread for them to take by night as they walk the woodland verge. Basajauns have thick legs with strange circular feet, and as they grow to adulthood often become lame in one leg, walking with the trunk of a felled tree as a walking stick and cudgel.
